diet_recommendations.item: At breakfast, replace white bread, maida upma or a large rice portion with 2 small jowar or bajra rotis plus 1 katori cooked moong sprouts or low-fat paneer sabzi; eat breakfast within 1-2 hours of waking.

diet_recommendations.item: Build lunch and dinner as 1 katori dal + 1 katori seasonal sabzi + 1 small millet roti or 1/2 katori brown rice; keep a 3-4 hour gap between meals and finish dinner by 8:00-8:30 pm.
diet_recommendations.rationale: Fibre and protein with controlled carbohydrate portions support steadier post-meal glucose and lower HbA1c.

diet_recommendations.item: Have 1 katori cooked oats or barley porridge 4 times a week at breakfast, and eat 1 katori salad before lunch and dinner.
diet_recommendations.rationale: Soluble fibre from oats, barley and vegetables helps lower LDL cholesterol.

diet_recommendations.item: Cook with 2-3 teaspoons total of mustard, groundnut or rice bran oil per day across meals; choose toned or low-fat milk and low-fat paneer; use 4-5 almonds and 1 walnut as a snack instead of fried snacks.
diet_recommendations.rationale: Replacing saturated fat from butter, ghee, cream and deep-fried foods with unsaturated oils and nuts helps lower total cholesterol.

diet_recommendations.item: At dinner choose 1 katori dal or sprouts + 1-2 katoris seasonal sabzi + 1 small millet roti; avoid eating rice and roti together at the same meal and avoid a heavy late-night meal.
diet_recommendations.rationale: A lower refined-carbohydrate load and avoiding late heavy meals can help reduce triglycerides.

diet_recommendations.item: For snacks use 1 medium guava or apple or 1 katori unsalted roasted chana instead of biscuits, sweets or fruit juice; drink water, unsweetened tea or unsweetened buttermilk.
diet_recommendations.rationale: Avoiding sugary snacks and drinks reduces glucose spikes and triglyceride production.

foods_to_avoid: Sugar, jaggery, honey, sweets, mithai and sweetened drinks including fruit juice and sugary tea or coffee
White bread, maida bakery items, refined-flour snacks and large portions of white rice at one meal
Deep-fried foods such as samosa, pakora, puri and chips; limit ghee, butter, cream and full-fat paneer
Processed and packaged snacks, sweetened breakfast cereals and fast food
Alcohol, if consumed, because it can raise triglycerides
coach.activity: Aim for 30 minutes of brisk walking on 5 days a week, plus a 10-minute easy walk after lunch and dinner. Start slowly if you are not used to exercise, follow your doctor's advice, and stop and seek medical care for chest pain, breathlessness or dizziness.
coach.sleep: Target 7-8 hours of sleep with a consistent bedtime. Avoid screens for 45 minutes before bed, and keep dinner at least 2-3 hours before sleeping.

diet_recommendations.item: Breakfast (7:30-8:30 am): 1 bowl (about 150 g) lightly steamed moong sprouts or 1 bowl of moong dal cheela (2 small cheelas, pan-cooked with 1/2 tsp oil) with 1 tsp lemon and jeera. Rotate with 1 bowl (40 g dry) plain oats cooked in water or toned milk, 3-4 days a week.
diet_recommendations.rationale: Soluble fibre from whole legumes and oats binds cholesterol in the gut and helps bring LDL down; this is also a light, Jain-friendly start to the day with no onion, garlic or root vegetables.

diet_recommendations.item: Lunch (1-2 pm): 2 jowar or bajra rotis (or 1 bowl, about 150 g, cooked foxtail millet) + 1 bowl (150 g) dal (moong, masoor, chana or toor) + 1 bowl (150 g) Jain sabzi such as lauki, tinda, parwal, bhindi, karela or palak + 1 small bowl of curd. Use no more than 1 tsp of mustard or rice-bran oil for the whole meal.
diet_recommendations.rationale: Replacing white rice and maida rotis with whole millets and adding a generous dal and vegetable portion lowers the refined-carb load that drives triglycerides, while keeping the meal within a Jain kitchen.

diet_recommendations.item: Dinner (7:30-8:30 pm, at least 2-3 hours before sleeping): 1 bowl (150 g) cooked brown rice or 2 small jowar rotis + 1 bowl (150 g) rajma, chana or lobia (not peanut) + 1 bowl of cooked seasonal sabzi. Keep dinner the lightest meal of the day.
diet_recommendations.rationale: A lighter, earlier dinner with legumes instead of a heavy rice- or maida-based meal reduces the evening fat and carb load that raises triglycerides, and legume fibre supports LDL reduction.

diet_recommendations.item: Daily at breakfast: 1 tbsp (about 10 g) freshly ground flaxseed (alsi) and 1 tsp chia or sabja seeds soaked in warm water. Also use 1 tsp sesame (til) seeds in chutney or sprinkled on sabzi.
diet_recommendations.rationale: Flaxseed, chia and sesame provide plant omega-3 (ALA) and fibre, which are among the most useful diet changes for lowering triglycerides in a vegetarian kitchen.

diet_recommendations.item: Mid-morning snack (11 am): a small handful of almonds (about 20 g, roughly 15 almonds) and 2 walnuts. Check the packet label to confirm no peanut or peanut traces; avoid all readymade mixtures and chutneys.
diet_recommendations.rationale: Unsalted tree nuts in measured amounts improve the blood lipid profile and are a safe snack for you as long as they are strictly peanut-free.

diet_recommendations.item: Afternoon/evening snack (4-5 pm): 1 whole seasonal fruit (guava, apple, orange, papaya or pear) or 1 bowl of sprout chaat with lemon and jeera. Always eat the whole fruit, not juice.
diet_recommendations.rationale: Whole fruit gives fibre and slowly released sugar instead of the rapid sugar load of juices and sweets, which is important for keeping triglycerides in check.

diet_recommendations.item: Sunlight: sit or walk in direct sun for 10-15 minutes between 11 am and 1 pm, 4 times a week, with arms and face exposed (no sunscreen for those minutes). Stop before the skin turns pink; skip the middle of the day if it is very hot and use early morning sun instead.
diet_recommendations.rationale: Regular short sun exposure is the main natural way to raise vitamin D, which is low at 15.22 ng/mL; your doctor will decide if any supplement is needed.

diet_recommendations.item: Vitamin D foods daily: 1 bowl (150 g) curd or 1 glass (200 ml) toned milk at breakfast, 30 g paneer 2-3 times a week, and UV-exposed mushrooms (button mushrooms kept in sunlight for 30 minutes, then cooked) twice a week. Ask your FOXO doctor before starting any supplement.
diet_recommendations.rationale: Dairy and UV-exposed mushrooms are among the few vegetarian foods that carry meaningful vitamin D and support correction of the low level alongside sun exposure.

diet_recommendations.item: Cooking and seasoning: use 3-4 tsp of oil in total for the whole day (mustard, rice bran, groundnut-free, or a little olive oil for salads). Use ghee sparingly, no more than 1 tsp a day. Flavour food with jeera, ajwain, haldi, hing, lemon and fresh coriander instead of deep-frying.
diet_recommendations.rationale: Cutting total visible fat and fried food lowers both LDL and triglycerides; this amount of oil keeps food practical and Jain-compatible without onion or garlic.

foods_to_avoid: Peanuts in every form: peanut butter, peanut chutney, groundnut oil, chikki, and any namkeen or sweet with peanuts or 'may contain peanut' labels
Onion, garlic, potato, carrot, beetroot, radish, ginger and other root vegetables (Jain diet) - use hing, jeera, ajwain and lemon for flavour
Honey, eggs, meat, fish and seafood (Jain diet)
Sugar, jaggery, sweets, mithai, halwa, pastries, cakes, biscuits, rusk, ice cream and sweetened drinks or packaged fruit juices - these raise triglycerides sharply
Deep-fried snacks such as samosa, kachori, puri, bhajiya, papad fried in oil and readymade namkeen
Bakery and maida items (bread, khari, puff pastry, naan) made with vanaspati or palm oil
Excess coconut oil, palm oil, butter and cream; keep ghee to about 1 tsp a day

coach.activity: Your doctor has not restricted exercise, but because your triglycerides and LDL need a cardiology review, stay with gentle activity only. Start with a 15-20 minute easy walk at a comfortable pace, building to 30 minutes, 5 days a week, preferably in the morning or early evening. Add 10 minutes of gentle yoga or stretching at home (simple forward bend, tadasana, seated twist) and light household activity. Avoid heavy weight training, high-intensity workouts and long fasted workouts until your cardiology review. Stop at once and contact your doctor if you feel chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations or dizziness, and follow all of your doctor's advice.
coach.sleep: Aim for 7-8 hours of sleep, going to bed and waking at the same time every day, including weekends. Finish dinner by 8-8:30 pm so there are 2-3 hours before lying down. Switch off mobile and TV screens 30 minutes before bed, keep the room dark and cool, and avoid tea or coffee after 5 pm. Poor sleep worsens triglycerides and insulin resistance, so treat it as part of your lipid management.
